title: Coupler Static Attributes
description: Distances are in meters, forces in newtons, impulses in newton-seconds, angles in degrees and speeds in meters per second. Rearm distance = max(capture_distance, rearm_distance_multiplier × lock_distance).

capture_distance.description: Capture range: closure force is applied while the endpoint distance stays within it.

lock_distance.description: Lock window: the connection is committed while the endpoint distance stays within it; it must not exceed capture_distance.

max_capture_force.description: Cap of the closure force in newtons. 0 closes only through existing actuators or outside forces.

lock_angle_tolerance.description: Allowed error between the two facing normals in degrees.

max_lock_speed.description: Allowed relative speed of the two endpoints at lock time, in meters per second.

rearm_distance_multiplier.description: Rearm distance multiplier; the product must be finite.

separation_impulse.description: Separation impulse in newton-seconds, applied to the part that leaves on release or on an unexpected decoupling. 0 switches it off. The impulse is blind to mass: 8 N·s is about 0.33 m/s on a 24 kg door, so heavy parts must set their own value.

separation_direction.description: Separation direction: a directional axis of the host subpart's local frame. Omitted uses the direction from the host mass center to the separation point; if the two coincide nothing is applied.

separation_command_only.description: true applies the impulse only when the coupler itself releases; false applies it on any separation.

separation_apply_on_center.description: false applies it at the separation point, lever arm included, so the part starts to rotate; true applies it at the center of mass for pure translation.

on_attach.description: Sound played once when the coupler latches.

on_detach.description: Sound played once when the coupler releases.

sounds.description: Basic lifecycle sounds plus one latch sound and one release sound; both default to the vanilla tripwire attach event.
